spouse_rule: No. Alaska's personal care rule says the state won't pay a personal care assistant who is the recipient's spouse, the parent of a minor recipient, someone with a duty to support the recipient under state law, or the recipient's representative. A court-appointed guardian can be paid only if a court authorizes the guardian to provide personal care services under AS 13.26.311(c) (7 AAC 125.010(b)(4)(B)). This rule covers Alaska's personal care services program only (7 AAC 125.010(a)).
other_relatives_rule: Not confirmed. Alaska's personal care rule, which covers the personal care services program only, bars paying anyone with a duty to support the recipient under state law (7 AAC 125.010), and Alaska law says each child is bound to maintain the child's parents when they are poor and unable to work (AS 25.20.030). We found no official Alaska page that says whether this stops an adult child from being a paid assistant. Ask the Alaska Department of Health before you count on it.
rule_quotes: "provided by a personal care assistant that ... is not the spouse of the recipient, the parent of a minor child who is the recipient, an individual with a duty to support the recipient under state law, the recipient's representative..." (7 AAC 125.010(b)(4)(B)); "Each child is bound to maintain the child's parents in like circumstances." (AS 25.20.030)
